items.stem: Which attribute marks a property so the engine tracks it for change detection?
items.explanation: [EntityProperty] tags a field for change detection; a property without it is not tracked.

misconceptions.d: [DuplicationKey] drives dedup matching, not change tracking.

items.stem: A teammate adds `[EntityProperty] public int Grade { get; set; }` to a POCO and runs start misbehaving. What rule did they break?

options.text: POCO properties must be nullable — it should be `int?`

items.explanation: Synnduit requires POCO properties to be nullable; a non-nullable `int` breaks change detection/loading. Use `int?`.

misconceptions.c: [EntityProperty] is fine on numeric types — the problem is non-nullability.

items.source: Documentation/Synnduit Requirement Poco Properties are Nullable.docx

items.stem: Write a minimal `Course` POCO: an [EntityType] (use any GUID and `typeof(SchoolObjectModel)`), a source identifier property `Code`, a tracked `Title`, and a `[DuplicationKey]` on `CourseNumber`. Remember the nullable rule.
rubric: [EntityProperty] on the tracked field(s) (e.g. Title, CourseNumber)

items.stem: Which attribute identifies the natural business key the engine uses to match possible duplicates?
items.explanation: [DuplicationKey] is the natural business key; the engine uses it to find a 'twin' destination record when there's no mapping yet.

misconceptions.a: The identifier attributes persist the mapping; [DuplicationKey] is what finds a duplicate.

items.stem: Why must every property on a Synnduit POCO be nullable?
rubric: Synnduit requires nullable properties as a hard rule
Non-nullable properties cause subtle change-detection / load problems (and it's not a compile error, so the bug is silent)
items.sampleAnswer: Synnduit needs every POCO property nullable; a non-nullable property (e.g. int instead of int?) breaks change detection and loading in subtle ways. It compiles fine, so the bug is silent until runs misbehave.
